title: LSTM lookback window and MLP forward pass English

textRun.content: LSTM lookback window and MLP forward pass
Architecture reference with equations and tensor dimensions

The MLP receives individual values from the recent window and a compressed LSTM summary of the preceding history. A recent outlier remains a separate input if its feature is included. An older value has no separate input here; its influence can survive in the LSTM summary and in recent derived indicators.

The following pages define the two branches, their timing, the LSTM recurrence, the exact join and every MLP matrix multiplication. The binary output describes the complete series under the fixed entry, stop, exit and re-entry rules.
Figure 1  Values for one decision at 13:05 UTC+3. Layer sizes and a 60-minute window are illustrative.
This is a proposed network specification. The existing Python script supplies data and targets; this document does not establish that the network has been implemented or trained.

Let d be the decision time, and t the index of the latest completed M1 candle available at d. The candle index refers to opening time; availability occurs at its close. At d = 13:05, t is the candle opening at 13:04. Set L = 60 and s = t − L. The older branch ends at 12:04; the recent window contains 12:05 through 13:04, inclusive.
Examples or aligned streams per batch
Older recurrent steps in one processing chunk
All older available steps since initialization

The current saved model schema contains 36 normalized market columns: nine features for each of M1, M5, M15 and M30. The nine are log price, log candle volume, RSI, relative ATR, MACD/ATR, signal/ATR, ADX, DI+ and DI−. It also contains 18 current main-anchor flags. Entry IDs, timestamps, raw OHLCV and future execution fields are excluded from that numeric model schema.

In this specification x_j is the 36-value market vector at minute j. Current anchor flags form a separate vector a_t. Historical anchor flags are not part of x_j in this example. Adding them requires explicitly changing F and defining their availability times.

Every higher-timeframe feature must use only a candle closed by the feature availability time. Normalization and any fitted scalers must be causal. Real zero values must not be confused with padding; missing values need an explicit policy.
The branches use different feature-row timestamps. Their underlying information can overlap: an RSI or ATR in the recent window may already reflect candles before s.

Use one unidirectional LSTM layer with no projection. For each older minute j, it consumes x_j and the preceding states h_(j−1), c_(j−1). The hidden state h is the exposed summary; c is the internal cell memory. The following uses column vectors and one combined bias per gate. [1]

The input gate i controls new information, forget gate f controls retained cell memory, and output gate o controls exposed memory. The candidate g supplies proposed new content. Each has H components. Multiplication marked ⊙ acts element by element.

Here * denotes i, f, g or o. With F = 36 and H = 64, each input matrix is [64,36], each recurrent matrix [64,64], and each bias [64]. Stacking four gates gives W_x [256,36], W_h [256,64], b [256]. These weights are shared across older minutes.

Only h_s enters the MLP in the baseline design. Both h_s and c_s are retained to advance the LSTM. The 64 numbers are learned coordinates, not 64 predefined indicators. Initialization defines the start of available memory; there is no guarantee of lossless or unlimited recall.
3 The recent window and the join

Construct the recent matrix directly from market feature rows. Rows run from oldest to newest; columns follow a fixed feature manifest. This is a parallel input branch: the recent matrix is not produced from the LSTM summary.

Each row contains all F features for one minute. Flattening places the first row into the vector, followed by the second row, and so on. It preserves every supplied value and its position. It does not average the window or compress it.

In the index equation j identifies a row within the recent window and q a feature column; indices start at 1. A single volume spike therefore occupies a specific vector position. The chosen feature may already be transformed: log volume preserves a positive volume value through an invertible transform, whereas an indicator alone does not reconstruct all raw candle fields.
Concatenate the recent vector, the older summary and the current anchor vector in that fixed order. Concatenation only joins values. Learned mixing starts in the first dense layer. [2]
Positions in z with zero based indexing

The current one-row feature export has 54 inputs. This proposed windowed network has 2242 inputs to its first MLP layer. Producing that input requires the complete minute timeline, not only the irregularly spaced anchor rows.

For a concrete example, use two hidden layers of widths 128 and 64, followed by one logit. ReLU is applied in hidden layers. Sigmoid converts the final logit into a number between 0 and 1. The architecture produces an estimated probability; calibration must be evaluated separately.
Partition the first layer by the three input blocks. Its pre-activation q₁ shows exactly where the LSTM output enters the calculation.

W_R has shape [128,2160], W_M [128,64], and W_A [128,18]. Thus each memory value can influence every first-layer neuron through a learned weight. It changes the activation values passed to subsequent layers. During prediction all weights remain fixed; the input values and LSTM states change. [3]
For a batch, examples are stored as rows of Z [B,2242]. This requires a transpose of the column-vector weights. Biases broadcast across the batch rows.
For B = 32 the layer outputs are [32,128], [32,64], [32,1] and [32,1]. One output represents two classes: class 1 has estimated probability p and class 0 has estimated probability 1 − p.
5 A numerical example of memory influence

Consider two samples with identical recent features and current anchor flags. Only one LSTM memory coordinate differs. The following chosen weights illustrate the arithmetic; they are not fitted model parameters or measured trading results.

Let the recent features, anchor flags and bias together contribute 0.3 to one first-layer neuron. Give memory coordinate m₁ weight 0.8. Pass this one active coordinate through an identity second-layer connection, and let the final logit be 2u − 0.2. All other relevant contributions are zero in this illustration.

The recent pattern is identical, but the older context changes the probability. The size and direction of this effect are learned. If the memory block weights are zero, its contribution to this layer is zero.

These partial derivatives hold the other supplied inputs fixed. A recent position n has its own first-layer weight. An older x_(j,q) acts through the LSTM summary. A raw-market change could also alter recent indicators through preprocessing. Later nonlinear layers can suppress either contribution. Direct access does not guarantee use of an outlier.

The LSTM cell equation also explains forgetting. Holding gate values fixed, the direct contribution of an old cell component is multiplied by successive forget gates. For example, 120 multiplications by 0.95 leave about 0.00212 of that contribution. This is an isolated arithmetic path, not the complete derivative of an actual LSTM.

A simple causal implementation maintains the LSTM exactly L minutes behind the latest completed candle. The recent window stores the most recent L feature rows. Each completed minute transfers the oldest recent row into the older branch.

After this update the new summary is h_(s+1). Remove x_(s+1) from the detailed window and append x_(t+1). The new MLP input still has 2242 values. No earlier candle is processed twice by this delayed recurrent stream.

An equivalent inference design processes the LSTM up to the latest minute and keeps snapshots. At decision t it selects the snapshot from t − L. With identical initialization and fixed weights this produces the same older summary. It must not accidentally supply h_t instead, because h_t also contains the recent window.
Advance the minute timeline even when no main anchor is active and while a series is open. Only the prediction and execution decisions are gated by anchors and position rules.
Save the model version, feature order, normalization settings, boundary index, h, c and the recent buffer for reproducible inference. After a model-weight change, rebuild states with that model.

Initialize from a defined history start and warm up before eligible predictions. Reset state at independent streams or replay from allowed past data; never carry a state computed from later candles backward in time.

A forward pass uses only input values and fixed current weights. Training additionally compares its output with a known historical outcome and updates weights. The MLP has no recurrent state of its own in this design. The recurrent feedback within the LSTM and the training feedback through gradients are different mechanisms.

Let R_net,t be the complete series return after the applicable execution and borrowing costs, expressed consistently with the threshold τ. The label equals 1 only when that return exceeds τ. Class 0 includes losses, breakeven and returns below the chosen minimum. A probability cutoff for admitting an order is a separate setting.

The existing field target_gross_return_pct is a gross series result, not this net binary label. Its legacy definition sums per-trade percentage returns. A future label builder must define costs, sizing and the return denominator explicitly. Unfilled initial orders and series with unavailable final targets must not silently become losses.

Use a mask v_t equal to 1 for main-anchor opportunities with valid targets and 0 elsewhere. Compute the following binary cross entropy only when the sum of the mask is positive. Non-anchor minutes supply context without receiving a negative label. In code, a logits-based loss is numerically preferable to explicitly taking logarithms of sigmoid output. [4]

θ denotes trainable weights and η the learning rate; the update is a simple gradient-descent illustration. The loss gradient reaches the memory coordinates through the MLP and then reaches LSTM weights through the recurrent computation. Both branches can therefore learn from the same binary target. An intentional detach or a precomputed frozen summary blocks that gradient at the boundary.

The three-dimensional input is a storage convention for batches of sequences. It remains useful for this hybrid design. Processing in chunks avoids rebuilding a separate full historical prefix for every anchor.

The state shape [1,B,H] follows the PyTorch convention for one layer and one direction; batch_first changes the input convention, not the state convention. A summary used in the MLP is selected from that layer as [B,H]. Padded sequences require true lengths or a valid mask. Padding zeros must not overwrite the state after the final real step.

K is the processed chunk length, not the detailed lookback length L. With truncated backpropagation, h and c may continue numerically across chunks while their earlier computation graph is detached. Thus retained history and the range over which an outcome can teach the LSTM are different. Detaching the entire older branch before every eligible loss prevents its end-to-end learning. [5]

Each persistent batch slot must continue the same chronological stream. Independent examples may be batched if each has its own correct prefix and state. Chronological evaluation must separate training outcomes from validation and test periods, including overlapping target intervals. Replaying allowed past inputs with fixed trained weights is compatible with causal evaluation.

The pseudocode below describes one stream and one decision. The feature timeline is already causal, finite and consistently ordered. h and c were initialized at the defined history start; older_cursor identifies the last minute already absorbed by the older branch. The loop also handles several new minutes between anchor decisions.
# t: last completed M1 index; x[j] has F values

Keep the current anchor flags tied to order placement time even if the initial order fills later. At 13:05, the latest closed M5 candle may create an anchor, while the 13:05 M1 candle has just opened and supplies no completed-candle features.

The first dense layer has 128·2242 + 128 = 287232 parameters; the second has 64·128 + 64 = 8256; the output has 64 + 1 = 65. Total MLP parameters: 295553. The canonical single-bias LSTM has 4H(F + H + 1) = 25856 parameters; total: 321409.

PyTorch stores two bias vectors per gate, so its LSTM count is 26112 and the combined count 321665. Summing its input and recurrent biases gives the effective bias used in the equations. These counts describe the example architecture, not evidence that it is appropriately sized for the available training sample.
Selected feature inside the recent window
Its separate transformed numeric value and exact lag position.
Selected feature before the recent window
Compressed influence via the LSTM; recent derived indicators may also retain indirect influence. Exact retrieval is not guaranteed.
Raw candle field absent from selected features
No direct value. Presence in an inspection spreadsheet does not add it to the network input.

If a particular older single event must remain explicitly accessible, add a defined event vector e_t. Examples are an event flag, its magnitude and elapsed minutes since it occurred, computed from past data only. This changes the model contract and dimensions; it cannot be assumed to emerge reliably from compression.

For E additional explicit values, the MLP input grows by E. Supplying both h_s and c_s instead of h_s alone would similarly change H to 2H in the join, giving 2306 inputs in this example. Such variants require their own training and evaluation.
Verify the exact s = t − L boundary, chronological flatten order, feature manifest and state-to-stream mapping. Check the emitted shapes against Section 8.

Exclude future fill prices, stops, exits, target values and future timestamps from inputs. Preserve all eligible hypothetical anchor samples; apply the chronological admission rule separately during execution evaluation.
Establish whether LSTM gradients actually reach older inputs during training. Compare the full model with the same recent-window MLP alone before attributing an improvement to older context.
